label: The Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs (Grosseteste's Latin, in English), 1791

volumes.title: The testament of the twelve patriarchs, the sons of Jacob. Translated from the Greek by Robert Grosthead, B.D. 1791

why: biblical register, not in the King James Bible, widely printed in America in the period
consensus: Composed in antiquity (2nd century BC to 2nd century AD, with Christian additions); reached English through a 13th-century Latin translation.

label: The Book of Enoch, tr. Richard Laurence from the Ethiopic, 1821

volumes.title: The book of Enoch the prophet : an apocryphal production, supposed to have been lost for ages, but discovered at the close of the last century in Abyssinia : now first translated from an Ethiopic ms. in the Bodleian Library / by Richard Laurence.

why: biblical register; the first English translation, published nine years before 1830
consensus: 1 Enoch, composed 3rd to 1st century BC; Laurence translated the Ethiopic manuscript Bruce brought to Britain.

label: The Apocryphal New Testament (Hone, from Jones and Wake), 1820

volumes.title: The Apocryphal New Testament
volumes.author: various

why: biblical register; early Christian texts outside the canon, in period translations
consensus: Texts of the 1st to 5th centuries; some were pseudepigraphic in antiquity (letters of Paul and Seneca), but all were composed in antiquity, which is the question here.

label: The Koran, tr. George Sale, 1800

volumes.title: The Koran, commonly called the Alkoran of Mohammed
volumes.author: Sale, George, 1697?-1736

why: scripture claiming revelation, translated from a non-European language
consensus: 7th century Arabic; Sale's translation of 1734, with his long Preliminary Discourse.

consensus: 5th century BC Greek; Beloe's translation with notes. The corpus holds two of its volumes.

volumes.title: The remains of Hesiod the Arcraean, including the Shield of Hercules
volumes.author: Hesiod

consensus: c. 700 BC Greek; Elton's verse translation with notes.

label: Kalidasa, Sacontala, tr. William Jones, 1792

volumes.title: Sacontalá; : or, The fatal ring: an Indian drama
volumes.author: Kālidāsa

why: ancient text from a non-European language, translated in the period
consensus: Sanskrit drama, c. 4th-5th century AD; Jones's prose translation of 1789.

label: James Macpherson, Fingal and other poems of Ossian, 1800

volumes.title: Fingal : and other poems of Ossian
volumes.author: Macpherson, James, 1736-1796

why: sold as translations of 3rd-century Gaelic epic; the best-known case of the period
consensus: Composed largely by Macpherson in the 1760s from fragments of Gaelic ballad; the Highland Society's report (1805) found no originals for the poems as published.

label: Thomas Chatterton, Poems supposed to have been written at Bristol by Thomas Rowley, 1794

volumes.title: Poems, supposed to have been written at Bristol, by Thomas Rowley, and others, in the fifteenth century
volumes.author: Chatterton, Thomas, 1752-1770

why: presented as transcriptions of 15th-century manuscripts, in invented old spelling
consensus: Written by Chatterton in the 1760s; shown modern by Tyrwhitt (1782) and Warton (1782). Old, not ancient; its spelling will strain OCR normalisation and every word-based test.

label: The Book of Jasher (Jacob Ilive, 1751), as reprinted 1829

volumes.title: The Book of Jasher: with testimonies and notes, critical and historical, explanatory of the text. To which is prefixed, various readings, and a preliminary dissertation, proving the authenticity of the work
volumes.author: Ilive, Jacob, 1705-1763

why: presented as a translation of the lost book of Jasher named in Joshua; biblical register; reprinted in 1829
consensus: Forged by Jacob Ilive in 1751, with an invented translator (Alcuin) and testimonies.

label: W. H. Ireland, Miscellaneous papers under the hand and seal of William Shakspeare, 1796

volumes.title: Miscellaneous papers and legal instruments under the hand and seal of William Shakspeare: including the tragedy of King Lear and a small Fragment of Hamlet, from the original MSS. in the possession of Samuel Ireland, ... 1796
volumes.author: Ireland, W. H. (William Henry)

why: presented as transcriptions of Elizabethan documents; exposed the same year
consensus: Forged by Ireland, who confessed in 1796; Malone's Inquiry (1796) exposed it. Old, not ancient.

label: Horace Walpole, The Castle of Otranto, 1782

volumes.title: The castle of Otranto, a Gothic story. Translated by William Marshal, Gent. From the original Italian of Onuphrio Muralto, ... 1782
volumes.author: Walpole, Horace

why: first presented (1764) as a translation of an Italian manuscript of 1529; the title page still names the invented translator
consensus: Walpole acknowledged it in the second edition (1765); a fiction device more than a fraud.
